result.title: LexPilot: Benchmarking the Proactive Interaction Ability of Legal LLMs with Laypeople in Chinese Civil Case Consultation
result.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have greatly assisted legal professionals. However, our empirical studies reveal that, when faced with underspecified consultations from non-experts, current LLMs often produce irresponsible responses with limited utility despite lacking sufficient case details for definitive conclusions. To better assist laypeople, legal LLMs must identify focal points of dispute and proactively elicit crucial context from users. Unfortunately, existing data resources often focus on interaction and response quality, offering limited insight into how proactive interaction affects LLMs' downstream claim-level judgment prediction in actual civil cases. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{LexPilot}, a benchmark linking proactive legal interaction to claim-level verdict prediction using authentic Chinese civil judgments. Constructed from 432 real-world judgments across 36 common causes of action, LexPilot comprises expert-reviewed pairs of complete and underspecified consultation histories with corresponding court verdicts. Experiments reveal that current LLMs struggle with proactive legal interactions in underspecified consultations, with downstream judgment prediction substantially underperforming that in the fully specified consultation setup (-23.84% on average). Further analysis identifies critical bottlenecks hindering these capabilities. Our work highlights the urgent need for more user-centered legal AI to better serve the public.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 LexPilot：基于 432 份真实中国民事判决、覆盖 36 类案由，构建专家审核的「完整咨询—信息不足咨询」配对及对应判决结果，用于评测法律 LLM 在信息不足时主动追问关键案情的能力，及其对诉请级判决预测的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 主动追问以补全缺失案情、以及信息不足与信息完整条件下下游判断的显著差距，可能为 LVR 中「何时补充视觉证据、证据不足下的判断与停止决策」提供评测范式与问题表述线索，属推测性借鉴，可供核查。
